findings.title: Variance decrease does not imply the claimed exponential transfer guarantee
findings.assumptions: Uniform subsets of N=20; singleton gains .4/.6 equiprobable; pair gains .9 for pair{0,1}, .45 otherwise; full gain .5; epsilon .25. Positive bounded gains, full>=pool mean and decreasing variance all hold.
findings.decisive_evidence: Increasing r from1/20 to2/20 decreases variance .01 to15309/14440000, but support width grows .2 to.45, Hoeffding bound grows .043937 to.539408, and tail grows0 to1/190. Separate deterministic gains show upper-tail guarantee does not ensure rank preservation.
findings.alternative_readings: An informal concentration-scale interpretation requires added stability assumptions. Empirical successful transfers not refuted. Displayed one-variable Hoeffding bound itself valid conditionally.
findings.core_dependency: Main Section3.2.4 repeats AppendixC.1 rate to justify informative low-cost probe feedback and sampling budget.
findings.impact: Invalid core theoretical justification; no claim of failed model scores or useless software.
findings.correction: Retain conditional one-sided bound; remove r-rate until bias/concentration assumptions proved. No complete replacement guarantee certified.
